title: Your professional pattern room: tools, fabric and flow

say: Your professional pattern room: tools, fabric and flow.
This is the video for module one of Advanced Tailoring and Pattern Making.
At advanced level you are not only sewing clothes. You are making patterns that must be repeated exactly, sometimes for twenty aso-ebi guests or a boutique order of thirty pieces.

panel.heading: Patterns that repeat exactly
items: Read the fabric before you cut
A room where work moves forward

say: Every curve must be smooth and every notch must match its partner. Use the longest curve that fits the line. A hip curve makes one smooth sweep on a princess seam, where a short French curve makes a wobbly line.

panel.heading: Patterns that repeat exactly
items: Read the fabric before you cut
A room where work moves forward

say: You will also learn to read fabric before you cut it, and to set up a workroom where each garment moves forward, never backwards.

panel.heading: Patterns that repeat exactly
items: Read the fabric before you cut
A room where work moves forward

say: A pattern only you understand is a draft. A pattern a cutter can use without asking questions is a finished pattern. Write the style, then the piece name and size.

panel.heading: What every pattern piece must say

say: Write the cut quantity, for example, cut 2 self, cut 2 lining, or cut 1 on fold.

panel.heading: What every pattern piece must say

say: Draw the grain line the full length of the piece, with arrow heads at both ends, so the cutter can measure from the selvedge at two points.

panel.heading: What every pattern piece must say

say: Use one notch on the front armhole and two on the back, so a front sleeve can never go into a back armhole. Punch dart drill holes about 1 cm inside the true point.

panel.heading: What every pattern piece must say

say: And state the seam allowance. If anything is missing, the cutter has to guess, and guesses cost fabric.

panel.heading: What every pattern piece must say

say: The lengthwise grain runs parallel to the selvedge, the finished edge. It is the strongest direction and stretches least, so most pieces are cut on it.
The true bias is the diagonal at 45 degrees. To find it, fold the crosswise edge along the selvedge. Bias stretches and drapes.
Hang a bias-cut skirt for at least a day before you level the hem, because the bias drops unevenly.
Cotton, linen and many ankara prints shrink when first washed. A fitted gown cut to exact size can become too tight. So test first. Cut a square of 50 cm by 50 cm along the grain.

panel.heading: The shrinkage test
items: Cut a 50 cm by 50 cm square on the grain
Wash and dry it as the client will, then press
Work out the percent and record it

say: Mark the lengthwise direction with a thread or a pen arrow.

items: Cut a 50 cm by 50 cm square on the grain

say: Wash and dry it the way the client will, for example hand wash and line dry. Then press it.

say: For example, Bisi in Ibadan tested a cotton print. The lengthwise side now measured 48.5 cm, and the crosswise side 49.5 cm.

panel.heading: The shrinkage test
items: Cut a 50 cm by 50 cm square on the grain
Wash and dry it as the client will, then press
Work out the percent and record it

say: 50 minus 48.5, divided by 50, times 100, is 3 percent lengthwise. Crosswise it is 1 percent. A 110 cm dress would lose about 3.3 cm after the first wash.
So Bisi washed, dried and pressed the whole fabric before cutting, and wrote it on the order card.

say: When orders grow, the problem is rarely sewing skill. It is flow. Tag every client's fabric with her name, order number and due date the moment it arrives.

say: Cut on the largest clear table, then tie all pieces of one garment together with its tag, zip, buttons and lining, so the sewer never searches.

say: Put a bright white LED lamp at each machine, and keep pressing close by, because you press after almost every seam.

say: Then finish, inspect and pack. For example, Hauwa in Kaduna timed herself and added an overlocker first, because it removed her slowest step.

say: Now the safety rules. Do not plug several machines and an iron into one extension board. Overloaded boards can overheat. Use a voltage stabiliser or surge protector for machines.

cards.d: Never plug several machines and an iron into one board. Irons draw a lot of current and boards can overheat.
Run generators outside, never in a closed room. The exhaust has carbon monoxide, which can kill without warning.
Unplug the iron when not in use. Switch off a machine before changing a needle or clearing a jam.

say: Run a generator outside, never in a closed room. Its exhaust contains carbon monoxide, which can kill without warning. Store fuel outside, away from a hot generator.

say: Unplug the iron when you leave the table, and test shiny synthetics on a scrap, because they can melt. Switch off a machine before changing the needle or clearing a jam.

say: To remember. Use the longest curve that fits the line, and label every finished piece fully. Test shrinkage on a 50 cm square before you cut.
Bundle each garment with its tag. And keep generators outside and boards never overloaded.
